head: ^usage: mhw funnel-review <period> \[--root <dir>\]$
why: The usage line names the command the caller typed: the shell original printed its file name, funnel-review.sh; the CLI prints mhw funnel-review. The exit code (2) and the stream (stderr) are unchanged and still compared.

head: ^usage: mhw funnel-review <period> \[--root <dir>\]$
why: Same as usage-no-period: an empty first argument is no period, and the usage line names mhw funnel-review instead of funnel-review.sh. The exit code (2) is unchanged and still compared.

head: ^usage: mhw funnel-review <period> \[--root <dir>\]$
why: Added, not a golden case: -h or --help as the first argument prints the usage line on stdout and exits 0. The shell original had no help: it took --help as a period name and printed a NOT-COLLECTED report for docs/funnel-review/collected/--help.tsv. A period named -h or --help is therefore no longer reachable. Held by the help test in test/method/funnel-review.test.js.
